profile.subseg: **Transformer bushings** — OIP (oil-impregnated) · RIP/RIS (resin-impregnated, dry) · High-Current; + retrofit; + Sukrut (broader transformer components)

bull_bear.body:
- **Fundraise approved up to ₹150cr; likely ₹100–110cr** — for 550kV capex + testing, brownfield, and optionally retiring ~₹28–30cr working-capital debt.
- **Debt-averse** (CMD personal preference) despite acknowledging debt is "mathematically better"; wants quality investors on cap table.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Constraints = supply chain + people** (niche skills, sector-wide attrition; vendor development takes ~6mo and vendors may divert to export orders). "Buttoned up for 2–3 years" otherwise.
- New-plant execution: type-test / teething risk — but FY27 revenue **not dependent** on RIP-core localization success.
- Potential lower-kV (<400kV) overcapacity at the **transformer** level (raised by an analyst) — mgmt: demand rising globally, and Yash de-risks via geography + import substitution.
- Geopolitics/war: not directly exposed (no exports to conflict zones, no input sourcing there); indirect oil/FX cost — passed through.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- **96% repeat order rate**, approvals in **60+ countries**, long qualification cycles = durable moat. Measured/disciplined ("not maximizing short-term volumes"); won't badmouth competitors. Debt-averse, prudent.
- Competitive set on RIP localization in India: **CG Power, Hitachi India, MIM (Massa Izolyator Mehru, Bhiwadi)** + Yash — 4 players. Chinese bushings never banned but Indian buyers prefer local.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **OIP, not just RIP, is in shortage** — capacity-limited at the autoclave; cross-checks a transformer-co comment that "OIP facing shortage." Demand is across OIP + HC + RIP.
- The greenfield's real prize isn't capacity, it's **removing the import/export restriction** tied to the Swiss core-tech licence (now a clean break) → opens RIP exports.
- Pricing power is *real this cycle*: management openly says it extracts better prices "when there is a shortage."
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Technological leadership: early and aggressive move into Resin Impregnated Paper (RIP) and Resin Impregnated Synthetic (RIS) technology, described as the global 'Gold Standard' for safety
- Singular specialisation: 100% focus on transformer bushings (unlike broad-conglomerate competitors), enabling superior customisation and faster R&D cycles
- Pre-qualified/approved vendor status with elite, high-barrier-to-entry entities such as PGCIL, NTPC, NPCIL and DRDO, plus several global utilities, creating a significant moat against new entrants
- Agile manufacturing capability to provide custom 'drop-in' replacements for brownfield retrofitting, described as a high-margin segment larger OEMs often overlook
- Established global supply network across 60+ countries, supported by a network of agents and channel partners
- Scalable manufacturing capacity via commissioning of a new Greenfield facility plus a planned expansion roadmap
- Long-term expansion readiness through strategic investment in additional land, supporting phased capacity expansion over the next five to seven years
- Strategic presence in the United States via a dedicated sales office, supporting global expansion strategy
- Domestic market leadership with close to a third of India's transformer bushing market (per Chairman's statement)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Demand & competition risk — A drop in demand for bushings or rising competitive intensity could affect the Company's growth ambitions; demand is closely linked to investments in power infrastructure and grid modernisation.
- Raw material & input cost risk — Specialised papers, resins, aluminium, copper and other critical materials are exposed to price and availability fluctuations that could materially affect operations and performance.
- Supply chain & import dependence risk — Dependence on certain imported components, including RIP/RIS-related inputs, can affect lead times, cost and responsiveness; the upcoming Greenfield facility and backward-integration initiatives are intended to reduce this dependence.
- Foreign exchange & export risk — Export growth exposes the Company to currency movements, trade barriers, certification requirements and geopolitical uncertainties.
- Working capital risk — Long project cycles and utility- or OEM-linked orders may result in extended receivable cycles and higher working capital requirements.
- Product quality & field-performance risk — Transformer bushings are mission-critical components; any quality failure can affect customer confidence, warranties and reputation.
- Technology risk — Changes in transformer technology, increasing adoption of advanced dry-type systems, and competition from large global players may affect the Company's market positioning.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Bushings (core):** FY26 7,200 units (~half OIP / half RIP+HC). Bushing ≈ **5% of a transformer's cost**; **7 bushings per transformer** (3 LV, 3 HV, 1 neutral).
- **Sukrut Electric** (acquired FY26): ~₹25–26cr rev now → target **₹150–160cr in 4–5 yrs (5–6x)**; broadens transformer-component footprint.
- **Retrofit:** ~6–7% of revenue, low-MSR / high-margin, growing with global reach.

business.body: Yash Highvoltage Limited, established in 2002 and headquartered in Vadodara, Gujarat, manufactures condenser-graded Oil Impregnated Paper (OIP), Resin Impregnated Paper (RIP) and Resin Impregnated Synthetic (RIS) transformer bushings, along with wall-through and oil-to-oil bushings. It also provides retrofit and replacement solutions for ageing transformer assets, supporting utilities and OEMs in enhancing reliability and extending equipment life. With over two decades of experience and more than 45,000 bushings supplied globally, it serves utilities, transformer OEMs, EPC players and critical power infrastructure customers across 60+ countries.

- **Wall-Through and Oil-to-Oil Bushings:** Wall-through bushings, Oil-to-oil bushings

outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **RIP/RIS core localization** (greenfield, Jarod nr Baroda): India imports ~95% of RIP capacitive cores → import substitution; design scope raised **220kV → 550kV**; +5,000–7,000 units high-value RIP/RIS; commercial RIP cores by **end-FY27**. Removes prior **export restriction** (own core = sell anywhere).
- **Higher voltage ladder:** now 420kV (India) / 550kV (global); **765kV / HVDC** open but only after 18–24mo of stabilizing the new plant.
- **Exports / US:** subsidiary operational; customers "waiting for the new factory" to qualify & order.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Long-standing strategy of localising dry-type RIP bushing technology in India, pursued for over a decade ahead of market readiness
- Greenfield facility in Vadodara to localise capacitive cores (currently ~95% imported by India) and lift voltage capability from 245 kV to 550 kV
- Broadened participation across the transformer ecosystem via a 50% stake in Sukrut Electric
- Direct international market engagement through wholly owned subsidiary Yash HV USA Inc., plus distribution partnerships across Europe (including UK and Ireland) and North Africa
- Grow exports as an increasingly important driver of future growth, aiming over the medium term to raise exports to a fifth or more of revenue by building a deeper presence in North America, Europe and other Western markets
- Measured, disciplined growth approach prioritising strategic opportunities that best leverage existing capabilities, while protecting the reliability/trust built with customers across 60+ countries
- Ambition to become one of the leading transformer bushing manufacturers in the world within this decade
- Elevated brand architecture and marketing initiatives (global forums, digital outreach, thought-leadership content) to support global market penetration and export growth
- Quality and operational excellence focus: obtained ISO 14001:2015 (Environmental Management) and ISO 45001:2018 (Occupational Health & Safety) certifications; enhanced in-house testing infrastructure (RIV, TRT, Dew Point Measurement)
- Expansion of OIP bushing range up to 245 kV to move further into the premium, higher-value segment of the transformer bushing market
- Board declared/proposed a dividend of ₹1.40 per equity share (face value ₹5) for FY2025-26, to be put to shareholders at the AGM. IPO/issue proceeds have been utilised in line with stated objects (setting up a new factory and general corporate purposes) with no deviation or variation in utilisation as at 31 March 2026. The Company has not accepted any public deposits during the year, and reinvestment has continued via inorganic moves — the 50% JV stake in Sukrut Electric, incorporation of Yash HV USA Inc., and acquisition of Yash HV Power Components Private Limited — alongside organic capacity expansion.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's flagship expansion project is a Greenfield manufacturing facility at Vadodara, Gujarat (a ₹153 Crore investment), intended to localise capacitive cores that India currently imports to the tune of ~95% of its needs, lift voltage capability from 245 kV to 550 kV, strengthen RIP & RIS capacity, enable backward integration into RIP/RIS core production, and support global competitiveness and future export growth. During FY2025-26 the Company also completed an expansion of its existing OIP manufacturing facility at current premises — extending the manufacturing area, commissioning high-speed wideband winding machines, installing new autoclave systems, and adding advanced assembly and oil-flooding stations — raising OIP manufacturing capacity to approximately 10,000 units per annum from around 6,000 units per annum previously. Separately, the Company has made a strategic investment in additional land to create a platform for phased capacity expansion over the next five to seven years. International capacity/footprint expansion includes the incorporation of wholly owned subsidiary Yash HV USA Inc. (direct sales/marketing presence in the US) and new distribution partnerships across Europe, the UK, Ireland and North Africa, alongside a 50% stake in Sukrut Electric to broaden manufacturing depth within the transformer component ecosystem.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global economy shifting from consumption-led to investment-led growth, with capital increasingly flowing into energy transition, digital infrastructure, industrial capacity and power systems
- India in a 'Capex-led' growth phase, with policy-led infrastructure investment across power, transport and urbanisation supporting sustained industrial expansion
- Global electricity demand grew ~3% in 2025 and is expected to sustain annual growth of ~3.3-3.6% through 2030, with global grid investment crossing US$470 billion
- India's electricity demand is projected to grow at ~6.0-6.5% annually through FY30, with peak power demand expected to reach ~277 GW in FY26, driving accelerated investment in transmission networks and grid modernisation
- Global transformer bushing market projected to grow from ~US$1.8 billion (2023) to US$3.0 billion by 2033 (CAGR ~5.1%)
- Indian transformer market estimated at US$3.0 billion (2025), projected to grow to US$4.47 billion by 2030 (CAGR ~8.33%), driven by the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), renewable capacity additions and transmission network expansion
- Technology preference shifting toward RIP/RIS (oil-free, lower-maintenance) bushings; RIP demand surged 22% YoY in FY26, driven by Green Energy Corridors
- Demand shaped by rising electricity consumption, transmission expansion, renewable integration, industrial electrification, data-centre growth, EV ecosystem development and replacement of ageing grid assets
- Power infrastructure sector entering a multi-year investment cycle where grid modernisation, renewable integration and transmission capacity expansion are translating into firm orders rather than mere intent
- Order book exceeding ₹400 crore as of 31 March 2026, providing strong revenue visibility over the coming years
- Order book grew from ₹150 crore (31 March 2025) to over ₹400 crore (31 March 2026) within a single year, offering multi-year revenue visibility that few peers of similar scale can match
- Company continues to secure prestigious export orders for High Current Bushings for execution over the next two financial years, a number earmarked for advanced data-centre projects of a leading global technology company headquartered in the United States
- Landmark order bookings for export contribution exceeded ₹22 crore during FY2025-26, a twofold increase versus ~₹11 crore of order inflows in FY2024-25
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Pure-play transformer-bushing maker riding a structural shortage — *"demand significantly exceeds global supply capacity across the bushing ecosystem"*, transformer OEMs placing **24–36 month blanket orders**. Record FY26 (+57% rev, 25.7% EBITDA), ₹400cr+ OB, and a **greenfield to localize imported RIP cores** (95% imported today) that lifts capacity ~10k→15k bushings (~₹700cr potential) and unlocks exports. Guides **40–45% growth**, margins held ~25% then expanding.

meta.thesis: Pure-play transformer-bushing maker riding a structural shortage — *"demand significantly exceeds global supply capacity across the bushing ecosystem"*, transformer OEMs placing **24–36 month blanket orders**. Record FY26 (+57% rev, 25.7% EBITDA), ₹400cr+ OB, and a **greenfield to localize imported RIP cores** (95% imported today) that lifts capacity ~10k→15k bushings (~₹700cr potential) and unlocks exports. Guides **40–45% growth**, margins held ~25% then expanding.
